To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the H2 type 6 secretion system (H6SS) of Pseudomonasaeruginosa strain PA01 delivers the VgrG effector to the host cell cytosol, which in turn interacts with the γ-tuRC, a microtubulenucleating center.
we discovered a new target for a bacterial protein, the γ-tubuline ring complex, and that this target promotes P. aerugiosa internalization in epithelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which P. aeruginosainvades epithelial cells.
the mechanisms by which P. aeruginosainvades human epithelial cells.
the molecular mechanisms by which P. aeruginosainvades human cells and, more particularly with the identification and characterization of the bacterial protein responsible for this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the γTuRC is the major host target for VgrG2.

the H2-TSS promotes P. aerugionsa entry in epithelial cells by delivering the VgrG effector into target cells where it binds to the γTuRC and triggers a microtubular-dependent internalization of bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel mechanism by which P. aeruginosainvades host cells.
we identified the bacterial protein VgrG2 as an effector that promotes Pseudomonas invasion into nonphagocytotic cells.
we identified the first bacterial protein interacting with microtubule and specifically with γTuRC, a multiprotein complex involved in microtubule formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the opportunistic bacterial human pathogen P. aeruginosais able to promote its own internalization into nonphagocytotic cells by a type of secretion/injection apparatus known as type VI secretion system.
VgrG is an effector that promotes P. aerugenosa internalization in non-professional phagocytes.
